summary: Field reporting from the Darién Gap in 2024 on migrants crossing the jungle between Colombia and Panama, the Emberá villages that receive them, and US-funded Panamanian deportations and border policies that make the route deadlier.

evidence.note: Introduced as a compilation of a week of It Could Happen Here episodes
Panama's new president vows to close the gap with US money; deportations funded by the US
Sexual assault on the trail and Panama expelling Doctors Without Borders after it reported it
Venezuela's disputed July 2024 election and economic collapse as drivers of migration
African migrants face anti-blackness and targeted crime along the route
Description of the Lajas Blancas camp as the frontline of US border policy
Families separated as men are loaded for deportation flights from Lajas Blancas
Lawyer explains CBP One and migrants stuck waiting in Mexico
Over half a million crossed the previous year (2023), more expected in 2024

notes: Crossover: a week of It Could Happen Here reporting by James Stout republished in the BtB feed; time and regions filled anyway. Story is reportage, not history, so covered_span is 2023-2024. Bajo Chiquito's 1965 founding is a passing mention. Deaths of children and sexual assault are mentioned repeatedly but not described in detail, so no content warnings were added; reviewer may want child-death.
